translationRepairs: In spring, the first month, on bingchen, Eastern Wei sent Acting Palace Attendant Li Jiang on a friendly mission.
In spring, the first month, on bingshen, Eastern Wei sent Acting Palace Attendant Li Jiang on a friendly mission.
丙申 is the sexagenary day bingshen; bingchen would be 丙辰, so the original day name is wrong and the proposed replacement matches the Chinese.
In spring, the first month, on bingchen, Eastern Wei sent Acting Palace Attendant Li Jiang as envoy.
In spring, the first month, on bingshen, Eastern Wei sent Acting Palace Attendant Li Jiang as envoy.
丙申 is bingshen, not bingchen (丙辰); the literal day name must follow the Chinese graph 申.
His sister, a descendant of Jingzong, and Zhongli's elder sister Dache were all Gao Huan's favored concubines, so their brothers went unpunished.
His sister, Jingzong's empress, and Zhongli's elder sister Dache were all Gao Huan's favored concubines, so their brothers went unpunished.
敬宗之後 identifies Wenchang's sister as Jingzong's empress (後 = empress), not a descendant of Jingzong; the replacement restores that sense.
His sister, a descendant of Jingzong, and Zhongli's elder sister Dache were all Huan's favored concubines, so their brothers were not punished.
His sister, Jingzong's empress, and Zhongli's elder sister Dache were all Huan's favored concubines, so their brothers were not punished.
敬宗之後 means Jingzong's empress, not a Jingzong descendant; the literal must use that court-title sense of 後.
In the third month, on yimao, Gao Huan entered court at Ye; the officials welcomed him at Zimo.
In the third month, on yiwei, Gao Huan entered court at Ye; the officials welcomed him at Zimo.
乙未 is yiwei; yimao would be 乙卯, so the original sexagenary reading is wrong.
In the third month, on yimao, Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan entered court at Ye; the hundred officials welcomed him at Zimo.
In the third month, on yiwei, Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan entered court at Ye; the hundred officials welcomed him at Zimo.
乙未 is yiwei, not yimao (乙卯); the literal day name must match 未.
Gao Huan took Cui Xuan's hand and praised him: "The court always had law officers—none would impeach.
Gao Huan took Cui Xian's hand and praised him: "The court always had law officers—none would impeach.
暹 is read Xian; Cui Xuan misreads 崔暹 and the proposed Cui Xian is the correct English form.
Huan took Cui Xuan's hand and praised him: "In the past the court certainly had law officers—none would impeach.
Huan took Cui Xian's hand and praised him: "In the past the court certainly had law officers—none would impeach.
崔暹 is Cui Xian; Xuan is an incorrect English spelling of 暹.
He gave Xuan a fine horse.
He gave Xian a fine horse.
賜暹 refers to Cui Xian (暹); English Xuan is the wrong reading of that graph.
He gave Xuan a fine horse.
He gave Xian a fine horse.
暹 is Xian; the literal recipient name must be Xian, not Xuan.
Xuan bowed; the horse bolted; Gao Huan himself caught him and gave him the reins.
Xian bowed; the horse bolted; Gao Huan himself caught him and gave him the reins.
暹拜 continues the same Cui Xian; Xuan is an incorrect English spelling.
Xuan bowed; the horse startled and bolted; Huan personally steadied him and handed him the reins.
Xian bowed; the horse startled and bolted; Huan personally steadied him and handed him the reins.
暹 is Xian; the literal subject of 拜 must be Xian, not Xuan.
Gao Huan came down the steps, knelt, and said: "Only Xuan is fit to toast; I also ask that the thousand lengths of my archery prizes be given him."
Gao Huan came down the steps, knelt, and said: "Only Xian is fit to toast; I also ask that the thousand lengths of my archery prizes be given him."
唯暹一人 names Cui Xian; English Xuan misreads 暹.
Huan descended the steps, knelt, and said: "Only Xuan can toast; I also ask that the thousand lengths of my archery prizes be given him."
Huan descended the steps, knelt, and said: "Only Xian can toast; I also ask that the thousand lengths of my archery prizes be given him."
暹 is Xian; the literal toast referent must be Xian, not Xuan.
Gao Cheng withdrew and told Xuan: "Even I still fear envy—how much more the rest!"
Gao Cheng withdrew and told Xian: "Even I still fear envy—how much more the rest!"
謂暹曰 addresses Cui Xian; Xuan is the wrong English spelling of 暹.
Gao Cheng withdrew and said to Xuan: "I still fear envy—how much more the rest!"
Gao Cheng withdrew and said to Xian: "I still fear envy—how much more the rest!"
暹 is Xian; the literal addressee must be Xian, not Xuan.
Yet Xuan inwardly carried a good deal of crafty deceit.
Yet Xian inwardly carried a good deal of crafty deceit.
然暹 continues Cui Xian; English Xuan misreads 暹.
Yet Xuan inwardly harbored much crafty deceit.
Yet Xian inwardly harbored much crafty deceit.
暹 is Xian; the literal subject must be Xian, not Xuan.

Cheng told Cui Jishu: "Cui Xian is sure to remonstrate bluntly; I have a way to wait for him too."

Cheng told Cui Jishu: "Cui Xian is sure to offer blunt remonstrance; I too have a way to wait for him."

When Xian came to consult on affairs, Cheng no longer showed him a pleasant face.
暹 is Xian; the literal consulter must be Xian, not Xuan.

After three days Xian let a visiting card fall before him.
暹 is Xian, so Xuan is wrong; but 懷刺…未得通公主 shows 刺 is a visiting card (名刺) for introduction to the princess, not a dagger, so the proposed after still mistranslates 刺.
After three days Xuan dropped a dagger before him.
After three days Xian dropped a visiting card before him.
暹 is Xian, so Xuan is wrong; but with 通公主 in the next unit, 刺 is a visiting card, not a dagger, and the proposed after still keeps that error.

Xian said fearfully: "I have not yet been presented to the Princess."

Xian said fearfully: "I have not yet gained access to the Princess."

Cheng was greatly pleased, took Xuan's arm, and led him in to see her.
Cheng was greatly pleased, took Xian's arm, and led him in to see her.
暹 is Xian; the literal must use Xian, not Xuan.

Jishu told others: "Cui Xian always hated my flattery; before the Great General he often said my uncle deserved death;
崔暹 is Cui Xian; Xuan is an incorrect English spelling.

Jishu told people: "Cui Xian always resented my flattery; before the Great General he often said my uncle should be killed;

Earlier, Eastern Wei's Prince of Gaoyang, Bin, had a concubine-born sister Yuyi whom the family disdained; she became Sun Teng's courtesan, and Teng cast her off;

Earlier, Eastern Wei Prince of Gaoyang Bin had a concubine-born sister Yuyi; her family disdained her; she became Sun Teng's courtesan, and Teng abandoned her;

Bo was the son of Bing.

Bo was the son of Biao.
